conflict_topics: unwashed shared pan / pork fat left in pan
cooking pork smells on weeknights / extractor and window use
stove time allocation / potential weeknight rota
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concise, context-grounded reasons (cost, sleep schedule, hygiene).
Key rule phrase 'who uses the pan washes it' is repeated across rounds (repetition score).
Agents make conditional, concrete proposals rather than vague promises ('try this week, set rota if fails').
No observable physical actions (e.g., washing the pan) are recorded; much is contingent agreement.
evaluation.final_reason: By round 6 the household agreed on a contingent, shared course of action: try the behavioural rule first and escalate to a formal rota only if it fails. Evidence: Agent A offered a conditional compromise ('I'm okay with a simple rota if we need one, but not right now. Let's try the 'who uses the pan washes it' rule first.' — Turn 11) and Agent D accepted that plan ('Okay, let's try the 'who uses the pan washes it' rule this week. If the pan is left unwashed again, we'll set the rota then.' — Turn 12). Agent A also committed to the extractor/window practice for pork frying ('I'll keep running the extractor when I fry pork.' — Turn 11). The immediate, concrete problem of last night's unwashed pan was not confirmed as washed, so that single instance remains unsettled while the parties settled on a process for ongoing behaviour.
position_change_notes: Agent A: initially defended cooking frequency but accepted extractor/window use for pork and the 'who uses the pan washes it' rule; later accepted conditional rota only if rule fails (Turn 3, Turn 11).
Agent B: moved from complaint to explicit agreement with the proposed wash rule and repeated extractor/window request (Turn 2, Turn 4).
Agent C: consistently pushed for immediate cleaning and hygiene; offered to wash 'this once' but refused ongoing responsibility (Turn 7, Turn 9).
Agent D: introduced new proposal (weeknight rota) in Round 5 but accepted the group's compromise to trial the wash rule first (Turn 10, Turn 12).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent A) highlights recurring smell and the unwashed pan and proposes a rule: 'whoever uses the shared pan washes it that night.' Turn 2 (Agent B) accepts that rule but adds a new demand about behaviour on weeknights: 'please avoid heavy pork frying on weeknights, or at least run the extractor and open the window.' A has not yet agreed to B's extractor/window request in this round, so incompatible expectations remain.

Turn 3 (Agent A) accepts B's extractor/window request for pork frying ('I'll run the extractor and open the window when I fry pork on weeknights') and reiterates the 'who uses the pan washes it' rule. Turn 4 (Agent B) repeats agreement. The main dispute is reduced to a minor outstanding issue (the existing unwashed pan and enforcement), since both parties have verbally accepted the proposed rule and extractor practice.

Turn 5 (Agent A) again affirms extractor use and the wash rule. Turn 6 (Agent B) asks for the extractor and window to be switched on now. No one has yet turned the extractor on, so a small practical disagreement remains about immediate action, but positions are aligned on policy.

Turn 7 (Agent C) directly demands immediate action: 'please switch on the extractor and open the window now. Also, whoever used the shared pan last night — wash it now, please.' Turn 8 (Agent A) agrees to switch the extractor but defers responsibility for last night's pan to whoever used it. The unresolved question of who left pork fat in a pan used by all remains explicitly contested and unsettled.

Turn 9 (Agent C) offers to wash the pan 'this once' but insists they 'can't keep doing that.' Turn 10 (Agent D) accepts the wash rule but introduces a new scheduling issue: 'Can we also set a simple weeknight rota so everyone gets fair stove time?' The dirty-pan responsibility is still unresolved and a new potential conflict (stove-time rota) appears.

Turn 11 (Agent A) accepts trying the 'who uses the pan washes it' rule first and agrees to keep running the extractor when frying pork; A says a rota is acceptable only if the rule fails. Turn 12 (Agent D) concurs: 'Okay, let's try the 'who uses the pan washes it' rule this week. If the pan is left unwashed again, we'll set the rota then.' These statements create a shared, conditional plan for future behaviour, reducing outstanding conflict. The immediate issue of last night's unwashed pan remains unresolved (no one confirmed washing it).

substantive_insights: Conflict involved at least three distinct issues: hygiene (dirty pan), nuisance (cooking smells affecting sleep), and resource allocation (stove time).
Agents prioritized a low-burden, behavioral rule first (who washes) before adopting a more intrusive scheduling solution (rota).
Conditional commitments (try rule, set rota if problem recurs) helped de-escalate by creating a clear trigger for further action.
Immediate accountability for the specific unwashed pan was not established; the dialogue focused on future prevention rather than retroactive resolution.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 6 because the final status is partially_resolved.
